newsitem.title: USA: Delaware businessman wins GOP Senate nomination.
newsitem.headline: Delaware businessman wins GOP Senate nomination.

text.p: Businessman Ray Clatworthy won the Republican nomination for the U.S. Senate Saturday, pitting him against incumbent Democrat Joseph Biden in the November election.
Clatworthy, 52, owns parternerships in restaurants, real estate and a radio station, as well interest in a credit card company that helps provide food for poor children.
Clatworthy defeated Vance Phillips, a farmer, and Wilfred Plomis, a businessman, in the primary with 81 percent with roughly two-thirds of the ballots counted.
The Republican opposes abortion rights, favours tax cuts and said he would run a campaign of "integrity. I don't care to get into personal matters," he said.
Biden was first elected to the Senate in 1972 at the age of 30 and has served as the chairman of the influential Senate Judiciary Committee.
